assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, substrate-limited problem into a routine operation. It is among the most used bond-forming reactions in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, with ligand design that is chemically original and conceptually clean. This is exactly the general-method, adopted-everywhere type of chemistry I value.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the catalytic, general amination with successively better ligand classes and mechanistic understanding. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling was a precursor but not the general catalytic method. A Buchwald and Hartwig pair is the fairest configuration, with Kosugi's precedent a possible footnote.
assessment.maturity: Mature: three decades of use, widespread industrial adoption and extensive mechanistic confirmation. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue, though the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize may make some members feel the area is already honored.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Exact weight of Kosugi's precursor contribution; I rely on memory of the history rather than verification.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and single-electron chemistry under mild conditions, giving new disconnections and late-stage functionalizations used throughout academic and industrial synthesis. The change in how chemists plan bond formation is large and general.
assessment.attribution: The 2008 reports by Yoon, MacMillan and Stephenson (with earlier Fukuzumi, Kellogg and Konig/Nicewicz work) make credit contested. The trio is defensible, but MacMillan already holds a 2021 prize for organocatalysis and the boundary with Nicewicz and Konig is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature in uptake, with many independent groups and industrial applications. Some intellectual debate remains on mechanisms and on how much is genuinely new beyond earlier inorganic photochemistry.
uncertainties: Prior laureate status of MacMillan may argue for a different trio.
Priority among 2008 reports and earlier photoredox precedent is disputed.
Reproducibility and mechanism questions for some photoredox claims.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization, particularly ligand and template-controlled Pd and Ir chemistry, changes retrosynthetic logic by treating C-H bonds as functional groups. It increases step efficiency, which is central to how I judge synthetic progress, and has been applied in natural product and drug synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-enabled and directed Pd chemistry, templates for distal selectivity), Hartwig (Ir borylation and others) and Sanford (Pd(II/IV) catalysis) made distinct decisive contributions. The credit is spread across many strands, so any trio is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Substantial adoption but still developing; scope and predictability are not yet routine in every setting, so recognition is slightly early compared with C-N coupling.
uncertainties: Overlap of Hartwig with B051 and possible double recognition.
The field is broad, with diffuse credit and several other major contributors not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation made total chemical synthesis of proteins practical by joining unprotected peptides chemoselectively. It was a clear conceptual advance in chemoselective bond formation, widely used for protein semisynthesis and modified proteins.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson (with Muir and Offord's precursor work) introduced and developed NCL. Kent is the central figure, with Dawson and Muir on closely tied lines of invention and application. Danishefsky's extensions are secondary.
assessment.maturity: Mature with decades of independent use, though it competes with recombinant methods for many targets, so impact is somewhat niche relative to cross-coupling.
uncertainties: Offord and Schnolzer precursor credit is not on the list.
Breadth of impact beyond specialist protein chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made reliable automated oligonucleotide synthesis possible, underpinning PCR primers, sequencing, synthetic biology and nucleic acid therapeutics. It is a synthetic methodology whose adoption is universal.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method; Hood is credited for automation and instrument commercialization, which is a distinct engineering contribution. A sole or near-sole award to Caruthers is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Extremely mature and in universal use, but recognition is long delayed; the Nobel committee may consider it already substantially acknowledged by other prizes and by the 2020s' therapeutic applications.
uncertainties: Contributions by Letsinger and Beaucage not shown on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolation of stable carbenes created N-heterocyclic carbenes as ligands and organocatalysts, strongly affecting metathesis catalysts, cross-coupling and main-group chemistry. A fundamental discovery that became a tool in synthesis.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo isolated the first stable NHC; Bertrand isolated earlier stable phosphino carbenes and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes. Nolan, Rovis and Bode are significant for applications rather than the founding discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature with decades of independent confirmation and extensive use, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand's 1988 carbene and Arduengo's 1991 NHC.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed metal-free activation of H2 and other small molecules, a conceptually new reactivity mode with applications in hydrogenation catalysis. It is chemically original, though practical impact on synthesis is smaller than the top candidates.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 H2 activation is the decisive result, and Erker contributed major expansion and geminal systems. The pair is clean.
assessment.maturity: Moderately mature; the concept is well confirmed, but industrial adoption remains limited and it may be a bit early.
uncertainties: Limited practical adoption relative to metal catalysis.
Earlier precedent from Tochtermann and Wittig on related Lewis pair behavior.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: RAFT polymerization gave a versatile controlled radical polymerization with wide monomer scope and tolerance of functional groups, widely used in polymer materials. It is a general method with broad adoption, although it is closer to polymer than to core organic synthesis.
assessment.attribution: The RAFT team at CSIRO (Rizzardo, Moad, Thang) was decisive and the three-person configuration is natural. Competition with ATRP (B046) may complicate how the prize area is framed.
assessment.maturity: Mature with widespread industrial and academic use, but the field of controlled radical polymerization has parallel inventions and the committee may prefer to treat them together.
uncertainties: Relationship to ATRP and nitroxide-mediated routes may require combined recognition.
My own expertise is in small-molecule synthesis, so polymer impact judgments are less certain.
